newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain convicts ex-spy for stealing dirty war files.
newsitem.headline: Spain convicts ex-spy for stealing dirty war files.

text.p: Spain's central military court convicted a senior military intelligence officer on Thursday of stealing secret files on a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatist rebels.
The court sentenced Colonel Juan Alberto Perote, former head of covert operations, to seven years in prison for stealing secrets that affected state security.
The court said that Perote had stolen 1,200 documents from the Spain's military intelligence department CESID when he was sacked in 1991.
The top secret files include some that are vital to state security and others that implicate the former Socialist government in the "dirty war" in which 28 people were killed.
The papers purportedly show that former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez and his associates set up undercover squads to combat separatist violence by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).

The scandal that broke when the papers were published in newspapers in 1995 led to a raft of resignations by top officials in the Socialist government and last year's election defeat of the long-ruling Gonzalez.
Gonzalez has consistently denied any knowledge of the undercover squads.

Perote is believed to have microfilmed the documents and destroyed a large part of the originals six months before he was fired. Officials say he eventually returned the files, although it is not clear whether he handed back originals or legally worthless copies.

In his defence the colonel, who has already spent 22 months in jail pending the trial, maintained that he did not deliberately steal the files. He said the documents were inadvertently put into his briefcase when he was fired.
He was arrested in June 1995 after the anti-Socialist newspaper El Mundo published excerpts from the documents.
